questions.stem: What is the purpose of a decimal point in the Indian place value system?
choices: To separate whole number from fractional parts
questions.solution: The decimal point in the Indian place value system is used to separate the whole number part of a number from its fractional part. This is a fundamental aspect of how numbers are structured in the decimal system. The other options describe mathematical operations or representations that do not align with the function of a decimal point.

questions.solution: 1 kilometer equals 1000 meters, and 1 meter equals 1000 millimeters. So, 1000 meters × 1000 millimeters/meter = 1,000,000 millimeters. 1000 mm is 1 meter, 10000 mm is 10 meters, and 100000 mm is 100 meters.

hi.stem: 1 किलोमीटर में कितने मिलीमीटर होते हैं?
hi.solution: 1 किलोमीटर के बराबर 1000 मीटर होते हैं, और 1 मीटर के बराबर 1000 मिलीमीटर होते हैं। इसलिए, 1000 मीटर × 1000 मिलीमीटर/मीटर = 1,000,000 मिलीमीटर। 1000 मिमी 1 मीटर के बराबर होता है, 10000 मिमी 10 मीटर के बराबर होता है, और 100000 मिमी 100 मीटर के बराबर होता है।

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of comparing two decimal numbers by place value?
choices: Comparing 1.23 and 1.32 by looking at the tenths place
Comparing 3.81 and 13.800 by looking at the units place
Comparing 1.009 and 1.090 by looking at the hundredths place
Comparing 2.7 and 3.5 by looking at the decimal points
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Comparing 1.23 and 1.32 by looking at the tenths place' because when comparing decimals, we start with the most significant digit. In this case, the tenths place is the first position where the digits differ (2 vs. 3), so we can determine which number is greater without looking further. The other options are incorrect because they either look at the wrong place or compare the numbers incorrectly.

questions.stem: If a decimal number has more digits, will it always be greater than a decimal number with fewer digits?
choices: Yes, because more digits mean larger value
No, because the digits after the decimal point can be smaller
Yes, because more digits always mean more precision
No, because the digits before the decimal point determine the value
questions.solution: The correct answer is no, because the value of a decimal number depends on the place value of each digit, not just the number of digits. For example, 0.123 has more digits than 0.2 but is smaller. The other options are incorrect because precision and the number of digits do not directly determine the size of a number, and the digits before the decimal point alone do not define the entire value.
